title: Creation of heaven and earth
summary: God creates, orders, and fills the world; humanity is made in God’s image.
chronology: Sequence in Genesis; no calendar year assigned.

title: Life in the garden
summary: The garden account describes human vocation, relationship, and the command concerning the tree.
chronology: Genesis 2 focuses on the human setting; traditions differ on its relationship to Genesis 1.

title: The human rebellion
summary: The man and woman disobey; the narrative follows their estrangement and departure from Eden.
chronology: Narrative sequence, not a dated event.

title: Cain and Abel
summary: Conflict between brothers culminates in Abel’s death and Cain’s exile.
chronology: Follows the garden narrative.

title: Noah and the flood
summary: Noah builds the ark; the flood is followed by a covenant with living creatures.
chronology: Genesis gives internal intervals; the absolute date and extent are interpreted differently.

title: Babel and the nations
summary: The tower narrative describes the confusion of language and the scattering of people.
chronology: Genesis 10 and 11 present the nations and Babel in different literary frames.

title: The call of Abraham
summary: Abram leaves his homeland in response to a promise of land, descendants, and blessing for all families.
chronology: Before Isaac and Jacob in the narrative; no precise BCE date assigned.

title: Abraham and Lot separate
summary: Their households take different paths; Lot settles toward Sodom.
chronology: A family branch within Abraham’s story, not a separately dated era.

title: Isaac, the promised son
summary: Sarah bears Isaac, and the narrative later describes Abraham’s testing.
chronology: The birth precedes the testing; Genesis does not state Isaac’s age at the testing.

title: Jacob becomes Israel
summary: Jacob’s flight, return, and encounter at the Jabbok shape the story of Israel’s ancestors.
chronology: These episodes are separated by Jacob’s years with Laban.

title: Joseph in Egypt
summary: Sold by his brothers, Joseph eventually administers Egypt’s food supply and receives his family.
chronology: Joseph’s Egyptian story overlaps his brothers’ life in Canaan.

title: Judah and Tamar
summary: Genesis interrupts Joseph’s story to follow Judah’s family and Tamar’s pursuit of justice.
chronology: Genesis 38:1 says “at that time”; exact synchronization with Joseph’s episodes is not given.

title: Moses is called
summary: After Israel’s oppression in Egypt, Moses encounters God at the burning bush and is sent to Pharaoh.
chronology: The text supplies narrative sequence; absolute dating remains debated.

title: Passover and deliverance
summary: The Passover instructions and departure from Egypt form Israel’s foundational deliverance narrative.
chronology: Early and late exodus chronologies differ; no one date is imposed.

title: Through the sea
summary: Israel passes through the sea and celebrates deliverance from the pursuing Egyptian army.
chronology: The crossing follows the departure from Egypt.

title: Covenant at Sinai
summary: Israel receives the covenant and the commandments at Sinai.
chronology: Exodus 19 locates arrival in the third month after leaving Egypt.

title: A dwelling among the people
summary: The tabernacle is erected and filled with the glory of the LORD.
chronology: Exodus 40:17 locates its erection in the second year.

title: The wilderness generation
summary: The spies’ report, Israel’s refusal, and the wilderness years lead toward a new generation.
chronology: Numbers describes forty years; the timeline card groups several episodes.

title: Crossing into Canaan
summary: Under Joshua, Israel crosses the Jordan and renews the covenant in the land.
chronology: Narrative order, without a fixed conquest date.

title: The cycle of the judges
summary: Judges describes recurrent oppression, cries for help, deliverance, and renewed unfaithfulness.
chronology: Regional judges may overlap; they are not plotted as an exact national calendar.

title: Ruth and Naomi
summary: A family returns from Moab to Bethlehem; Ruth’s story leads into David’s ancestry.
chronology: Ruth 1:1 explicitly places the story in the days of the judges, without naming a particular judge.

title: Samuel and the demand for a king
summary: Samuel’s ministry bridges the judges and the monarchy; the people ask for a king.
chronology: Samuel’s life overlaps the transition to monarchy.

title: Saul becomes king
summary: Saul is anointed and publicly recognized as king over Israel.
chronology: No exact reign dates imposed.

title: The death of Saul
summary: Saul and his sons die after the battle with the Philistines at Mount Gilboa. Samuel and Chronicles recount the same episode.
chronology: The Gilboa battle precedes David’s rule over all Israel. The Samuel and Chronicles passages are parallel accounts; no absolute year is assigned.

title: David and Jerusalem
summary: David rules over all Israel, takes Jerusalem, and receives a dynastic promise.
chronology: David first rules Judah before ruling all Israel.

title: Solomon and the temple
summary: Solomon builds and dedicates the temple in Jerusalem.
chronology: 1 Kings 6:1 supplies a relative interval from the exodus; its historical use is debated.

title: One people, two kingdoms
summary: After Solomon, Rehoboam and Jeroboam lead the southern and northern kingdoms.
chronology: The division begins two overlapping royal histories.

title: Elijah in the northern kingdom
summary: Elijah confronts Ahab’s kingdom and calls the people to allegiance to the LORD.
chronology: Set within Ahab’s reign.

title: Jehoshaphat in Judah
summary: Judah’s king joins Ahab in a military alliance despite Micaiah’s warning.
chronology: 1 Kings 22 explicitly places Jehoshaphat and Ahab together.

title: Elisha’s prophetic ministry
summary: Elisha succeeds Elijah and ministers during the history of the northern kingdom.
chronology: Elijah’s departure precedes Elisha’s independent ministry in the narrative.

title: Prophetic voices: Amos and Hosea
summary: Prophets address injustice and covenant unfaithfulness during Israel’s later monarchy.
chronology: Their superscriptions name overlapping royal settings; individual oracles cannot all be synchronized.

title: The fall of Samaria
summary: The Assyrian conquest brings the northern kingdom to an end in the narrative of Kings.
chronology: 2 Kings 18:9–10 synchronizes the siege with Hezekiah and Hoshea.

title: Hezekiah and the Assyrian threat
summary: Assyria threatens Jerusalem; Hezekiah seeks the LORD and receives Isaiah’s message.
chronology: Kings and Isaiah preserve parallel narratives of this crisis.

title: Josiah and the book of the law
summary: The discovery of the law leads to covenant renewal and reform in Judah.
chronology: Placed before Judah’s final kings and Jerusalem’s destruction.

title: Jerusalem falls
summary: Babylon besieges Jerusalem, destroys the temple, and deports inhabitants.
chronology: Kings and Jeremiah describe this same fall; calendar conversion is not encoded.

title: Faithfulness in Babylon
summary: Daniel and his companions serve under foreign kings while maintaining their allegiance to God.
chronology: Daniel’s book groups court narratives and visions; chapter order is not entirely chronological.

title: Hope among the exiles
summary: Ezekiel receives visions among the deportees and speaks of restoration and renewed life.
chronology: Ezekiel dates visions relative to the exile of Jehoiachin.

title: A letter to the exiles
summary: Jeremiah writes from Jerusalem to those already deported, urging them to seek their city’s welfare.
chronology: The letter explicitly connects Jerusalem and the Babylonian exiles before the final destruction.

title: Return and rebuilding
summary: Cyrus’s decree opens the way for return, and the Jerusalem temple is eventually rebuilt.
chronology: Ezra names Cyrus and Darius; the events span more than one reign.

title: Haggai and Zechariah encourage rebuilding
summary: Prophetic encouragement accompanies the renewed work on the temple.
chronology: Ezra 5 explicitly names both prophets in the rebuilding setting.

title: Esther in Persia
summary: Esther and Mordecai act amid a threat to the Jewish communities of the Persian Empire.
chronology: The narrative names Ahasuerus; identification and alignment with Ezra–Nehemiah involve historical reconstruction.

title: Jerusalem’s walls and renewed covenant
summary: Nehemiah oversees rebuilding the walls, and the community gathers to hear the law.
chronology: Nehemiah dates his mission to Artaxerxes; this is later than the temple rebuilding.

title: Job: suffering and understanding
summary: Job and his companions wrestle with suffering, justice, and the limits of human knowledge.
chronology: Job is not assigned to a patriarchal date: the text does not establish one.

title: Prayer, praise, and lament
summary: The Psalms collect many voices and settings of worship, grief, trust, and hope.
chronology: A collection across different settings, not one event or one date.

title: Wisdom for everyday life
summary: Wisdom literature explores conduct, love, meaning, and life before God.
chronology: Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Song of Solomon are distinct works, grouped here by literary theme.

title: The birth of Jesus
summary: Matthew and Luke tell distinct accounts surrounding Jesus’s birth.
chronology: The narratives do not provide an uncontested shared calendar date; their details are not forced into a single sequence.

title: Jesus is baptized
summary: Jesus comes to John at the Jordan; the Synoptic Gospels describe his baptism.
chronology: John recounts the Baptist’s testimony to the Spirit, rather than narrating the baptism directly.

title: Testing in the wilderness
summary: Jesus is tested in the wilderness before his public ministry unfolds.
chronology: Matthew and Luke present the temptations in different orders.

title: Teaching the way of the kingdom
summary: Jesus teaches on blessing, prayer, love, and life in the kingdom of God.
chronology: Matthew’s sermon on the mount and Luke’s sermon on a level place share material; identity of the occasion is debated.

title: Feeding the five thousand
summary: All four Gospels recount Jesus feeding a crowd with five loaves and two fish.
chronology: This is distinguished from the feeding of the four thousand in Matthew 15 and Mark 8.

title: The transfiguration
summary: Peter, James, and John witness Jesus in glory with Moses and Elijah.
chronology: The accounts use different day-count expressions; no calendar date is assigned.

title: Jesus enters Jerusalem
summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem amid acclamation, approaching the final conflict of his ministry.
chronology: The final-week narratives overlap, while details and arrangement differ.

title: The last supper
summary: Jesus shares a final meal with his disciples; the accounts emphasize covenant, service, and remembrance.
chronology: The relationship between John’s Passover chronology and the Synoptics is disputed.

title: The crucifixion
summary: The four Gospels narrate Jesus’s execution under Pontius Pilate and his burial.
chronology: The day and hour details are not harmonized into a single precise timestamp.

title: The resurrection witnesses
summary: The Gospels report the empty tomb and encounters with the risen Jesus, with distinct selections of witnesses and scenes.
chronology: Mark 16:9–20 has a significant manuscript-history question. The parallel anchor here ends at verse 8.

title: Witness to the ends of the earth
summary: Acts opens with the risen Jesus commissioning his followers and ascending.
chronology: Acts 1:3 describes forty days of appearances.

title: Pentecost
summary: The Spirit comes upon the gathered disciples; Peter speaks and a community forms.
chronology: Acts places this on the day of Pentecost after the ascension.

title: Witness beyond Jerusalem
summary: After Stephen’s death, scattered believers carry the message into new places.
chronology: Acts follows several people and places during the expanding mission.

title: Saul’s encounter on the road
summary: Saul encounters Jesus on the way to Damascus and begins proclaiming him.
chronology: Acts retells the encounter in later speeches; these are not three different conversions.

title: Peter and Cornelius
summary: Peter enters a Gentile household, and the Spirit comes upon those who hear.
chronology: Acts 10 narrates interlocking visions and a meeting; Acts 11 retells the episode.

title: Journeys and new communities
summary: Paul and his companions travel, teach, and establish communities across the eastern Mediterranean.
chronology: This card groups multiple journeys; letter dates are not inferred automatically from book order.

title: The Jerusalem council
summary: The church considers the place of Gentile believers and issues a letter.
chronology: How this visit relates to Galatians 2 is debated; the identification is not imposed.

title: Paul in Rome
summary: Acts closes with Paul receiving visitors and teaching while under guard in Rome.
chronology: Acts ends here without narrating Paul’s death.

title: Letters to the churches
summary: The letters address faith, conduct, worship, suffering, and hope in particular communities.
chronology: A thematic shelf, not a single moment. Authorship and dating of some letters are disputed.

title: John’s vision on Patmos
summary: John introduces his vision and messages to seven churches.
chronology: The visions address named churches; traditions differ on how their scope extends through history.

title: Judgment and the defeat of evil
summary: Revelation depicts the defeat of evil, a millennium, resurrection, and judgment.
chronology: Premillennial, amillennial, and postmillennial readings differ. Literary sequence is not presented as a universally agreed schedule.

title: A new heaven and a new earth
summary: The vision culminates in God dwelling with humanity, the removal of death, and the river and tree of life.
chronology: A vision of consummation; no predicted calendar date is supplied.
